    The "Commit failed" error on GitHub's website is a common glitch, often caused by a network timeout or a temporary browser issue. Since your index.html is about 460KB, it's well within the limits.

    Here are the three ways to fix this, starting with the easiest:

    1. The "Web VS Code" Trick (Most Reliable)

    This uses GitHub’s built-in editor, which is much more stable than the drag-and-drop uploader.

    1. Go to your repository page (Dinulkar.github.io) on GitHub.
    2. Press the . (period) key on your keyboard. This will transform your browser into a web-based VS Code.
    3. Drag and drop your index.html file from your computer directly into the file list on the left.
    4. Click the Source Control icon on the far left (it looks like a branch with a circle).
    5. Type "Initial commit" in the message box and click the Commit & Push button.
    6. Once it's done, you can close that tab and go back to your repository.

    2. Add a README first

    Sometimes GitHub's uploader fails on a completely empty repository.

    1. On your main repo page, click the "Add a README" button at the bottom.
    2. Scroll down and click Commit changes.
    3. Now that the repo has one file, try the Upload files button again for your index.html.

    3. Use the Terminal (Option B from before)

    If you are currently in the coding editor talking to me, you can use the Terminal right here to push the code properly. This is the "professional" way and won't fail.

    Run these commands one by one (replace YOUR_TOKEN with a GitHub Personal Access Token if you have one, or just use your password when prompted):

    Bash
    git init
git add .
git commit -m "Deploying CV Portfolio"
git branch -M main
git remote add origin https://github.com/Dinulkar/Dinulkar.github.io.git
git push -u origin main

    Why Option 3 is best:
    Since I added the .github/workflows/deploy.yml file to your project, if you use the Terminal to push the whole project, GitHub will automatically build and update your site every time you change your details in the future. You won't have to manually upload index.html ever again.

    Checklist:

    • Is the repository name exactly Dinulkar.github.io? (Capitalization doesn't matter, but the .github.io part is required).
    • Is the repository Public? (Private repos require a paid plan for GitHub Pages).

    yaml
    name: Deploy to GitHub Pageson:  push:    branches: [main]  workflow_dispatch:permissions:  contents: read  pages: write  id-token: writeconcurrency:  group: pages  cancel-in-progress: truejobs:  build:    runs-on: ubuntu-latest    steps:      - uses: actions/checkout@v4      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4        with:          node-version: 20      - run: npm ci      - run: npm run build      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3        with:          path: ./dist  deploy:    needs: build    runs-on: ubuntu-latest    environment:      name: github-pages      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}    steps:      - id: deployment        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

    Then Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions.

      Bash

git add .
git commit -m "CV portfolio v1"
git branch -M main
git remote add origin https://github.com/Dinulkar/Dinulkar.github.io.git
git push -u origin main

      (Create the Dinulkar.github.io Public repo on GitHub first if you haven't.)

    2. Enable Pages: In your repo → Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source → select "GitHub Actions".

    3. Done — every git push to main automatically builds and publishes to https://dinulkar.github.io. Watch progress under the Actions tab.

    const [lines, setLines] = useState<Line[]>([]); // completed lines: {type:'cmd'|'out', text}const [typing, setTyping] = useState("");useEffect(() => {  let li = 0, ci = 0, cancelled = false; let timer: number;  const tick = () => {    if (cancelled) return;    if (li >= script.length) { timer = window.setTimeout(() => { if(!cancelled){ setLines([]); setTyping(""); li=0; ci=0; tick(); } }, 6000); return; }    const { cmd, out } = script[li];    if (ci <= cmd.length) { setTyping(cmd.slice(0, ci)); ci++; timer = window.setTimeout(tick, 55 + Math.random()*50); }    else {      // push command line      setLines(prev => [...prev, { type: "cmd", text: cmd }]);      setTyping("");      // then outputs staggered      out.forEach((o, i) => { timer = window.setTimeout(() => { if(!cancelled) setLines(prev => [...prev, {type:"out", text:o}]); }, 250*(i+1)); });      li++; ci = 0;      timer = window.setTimeout(tick, 250*out.length + 500);    }  };  timer = window.setTimeout(tick, 600);  return () => { cancelled = true; clearTimeout(timer); };}, []);

    Count-up:

    ts
    export function useCountUp(target: number, active: boolean, duration = 1600) {  const [val, setVal] = useState(0);  useEffect(() => {    if (!active) return;    let raf: number; const t0 = performance.now();    const step = (t: number) => {      const p = Math.min(1, (t - t0) / duration);      const e = 1 - Math.pow(1 - p, 4);      setVal(Math.round(target * e));      if (p < 1) raf = requestAnimationFrame(step);    };    raf = requestAnimationFrame(step);    return () => cancelAnimationFrame(raf);  }, [active, target, duration]);  return val;}

    const WEEKS = 53;export function buildContributions(seed = 42) {  const rand = mulberry32(seed);  const today = new Date();   const end = new Date(today); end.setDate(end.getDate() + (6 - end.getDay())); // end of current week (Sat)  const start = new Date(end); start.setDate(start.getDate() - (WEEKS*7 - 1));  const grid: { count:number; level:number; date:string; future:boolean }[][] = [];  let total = 0;  for (let w = 0; w < WEEKS; w++) {    const col = [];    for (let d = 0; d < 7; d++) {      const date = new Date(start); date.setDate(start.getDate() + w*7 + d);      const future = date > today;      const r = rand();      let count = 0;      const dow = date.getDay();      const weekend = dow === 0 || dow === 6;      if (!future) {        if (r < (weekend ? 0.55 : 0.18)) count = 0;        else if (r < 0.6) count = 1 + Math.floor(rand()*3);        else if (r < 0.85) count = 4 + Math.floor(rand()*4);        else if (r < 0.96) count = 8 + Math.floor(rand()*5);        else count = 13 + Math.floor(rand()*8);        // vacation gap        if (w >= 28 && w <= 29 && rand() < 0.8) count = 0;      }      const level = count === 0 ? 0 : count < 4 ? 1 : count < 8 ? 2 : count < 13 ? 3 : 4;      total += count;      col.push({ count, level, date: date.toLocaleDateString("en-US", { month:"short", day:"numeric", year:"numeric" }), future });    }    grid.push(col);  }  return { grid, total };}
